related_questions.question: What does a clogged artery feel like in the chest?

text_blocks.snippet: A clogged artery in the chest, which often manifests as angina, can feel like a pressure, squeezing, or tightness in the chest. It may also be described as a dull ache, burning, or heaviness. The pain can radiate to the arms, neck, jaw, back, or shoulders. Shortness of breath, fatigue, nausea, and dizziness can also accompany the chest discomfort.
snippet_highlighted_words: a pressure, squeezing, or tightness in the chest

list.snippet: Location: Primarily under the breastbone, but can spread to other areas.
Sensation: Described as pressure, squeezing, tightness, or a heavy feeling.
Duration: Angina pain usually subsides with rest or medication, while heart attack pain may not.
Shortness of breath: Feeling like you can't get enough air.
Fatigue: Feeling unusually tired or weak.
Dizziness or lightheadedness: Especially during physical activity.
Nausea or vomiting: Can occur, sometimes mistaken for indigestion.
Sweating: Cold sweats can be a sign.

list.title: Angina vs. Heart Attack:
list.snippet: While both can involve chest pain, heart attack pain is often more severe and doesn't subside with rest. If symptoms persist for more than 10-15 minutes, seek immediate medical attention.

list.title: Silent Heart Attacks:
list.snippet: Some individuals, especially those with diabetes or older adults, may experience a heart attack without noticeable chest pain.

list.title: Individual Variation:
list.snippet: Symptoms can vary from person to person, and women may experience angina differently than men.
Any new or worsening chest pain or discomfort, especially if accompanied by other symptoms like shortness of breath or sweating.
If you think you might be having a heart attack, call emergency services immediately.

related_questions.question: How do I check if my arteries are clogged?

text_blocks.snippet: You can't check for clogged arteries at home; it requires medical tests. Doctors use imaging tests like CT scans, MRIs, or angiograms to visualize blood vessels and identify blockages. Additionally, they may order blood tests to assess risk factors.
Here's a breakdown of how doctors diagnose clogged arteries:

list.title: Angiogram:
list.snippet: This invasive procedure involves inserting a catheter into an artery and injecting a dye that allows doctors to visualize blood flow and identify blockages using X-rays.

list.title: CT Angiogram:
list.snippet: This non-invasive test uses a CT scanner and contrast dye to create detailed 3D images of the heart's arteries.

list.title: MRI Angiogram:
list.snippet: This test uses magnetic resonance imaging to visualize blood vessels and detect blockages or narrowing.

list.title: Echocardiogram:
list.snippet: This ultrasound test provides images of the heart's structure and function, which can help identify blockages.

list.title: Blood tests:
list.snippet: These tests can assess risk factors for clogged arteries, such as high cholesterol or blood sugar levels.

text_blocks.snippet: Symptoms of clogged arteries may include:

list.snippet: Chest pain or discomfort
Shortness of breath
Fatigue
Dizziness or lightheadedness
Pain or numbness in the extremities
Slow-healing sores or ulcers

text_blocks.snippet: If you are concerned about clogged arteries, it is best to consult with a doctor for proper diagnosis and treatment.

text_blocks.snippet: Clogged arteries in the chest, particularly those supplying the heart (coronary arteries), can cause a variety of symptoms, with chest pain (angina) being the most prominent. Other symptoms include shortness of breath, fatigue, and abnormal heart rhythms. In some cases, blocked arteries can also lead to nausea, sweating, and pain in the arms or jaw.
snippet_highlighted_words: chest pain (angina) being the most prominent.
Other symptoms include shortness of breath, fatigue, and abnormal heart rhythms

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a more detailed look at the symptoms:

list.title: Chest Pain (Angina):
list.snippet: This is often described as a squeezing, pressure, or tightness in the chest, and it can radiate to the arms, jaw, neck, or back. The pain usually occurs during physical activity or stress and subsides with rest.

list.title: Shortness of Breath:
list.snippet: This can occur with exertion or even at rest, as the heart struggles to pump enough blood to meet the body's needs.

list.title: Fatigue:
list.snippet: Feeling unusually tired or weak, even with minimal physical activity, can be a sign of clogged arteries.

list.title: Abnormal Heart Rhythms:
list.snippet: The heart may beat too fast, too slow, or irregularly (palpitations).

list.title: Nausea and Vomiting:
list.snippet: These symptoms can occur, particularly during episodes of angina or exertion.

list.title: Cold Sweats:
list.snippet: Sudden, excessive sweating, especially when not associated with physical exertion, can be a warning sign.

list.title: Pain in the Arms or Shoulders:
list.snippet: Discomfort or pain in the arms, shoulders, or jaw can accompany chest pain or occur on its own.

list.title: Lightheadedness or Dizziness:
list.snippet: These symptoms can be related to reduced blood flow to the brain.

text_blocks.snippet: It's crucial to seek immediate medical attention if you experience any of these symptoms, especially chest pain, shortness of breath, or sudden onset of dizziness or weakness. Early diagnosis and treatment are essential to prevent serious complications like heart attack or stroke.
